message:
Hi Danielle Cathleen,

First of all let me express to you my condolence to you at the passing of your Mother. I'm sorry that you had to go through this with these two companies. May I suggest that you file a complaint online with the MD PSC.
By no means give them your social security number. In your complaint please mention the fact that they have your information together with Evercom. Demand that the PSC get a detailed list of your call history. This is what happened to me. My T-NETIX call history was on an Evercom customer care list. I complained about this because I didn't know that I was an Evercom customer until I got the call list. When my son came to court in Upper Marlboro it turns out that Evercom has the contract for the local jail. The problem lies in the Correctional Billing Service part. It does not matter what state or what telephone provider that you have, if CBS does the billing for the provider then you are bound by CBS.

When you file your complaint with the PSC T-NETIX will have to respond to you in writing. The first thing they will declare to you is that an account was set up for you when you accepted your first telephone call from a correctional that has a billing arrangement with CBS. They will tell you that you are assigned a PVP for a certain dollar amount. You will not know this information until you file that PSC complaint. It will also tell you if you exceed a certain number of calls in one day. They will tell you that it is to prevent fraud. That's a joke, they are the biggest crooks in the world.

This is how you truly understand how they operate when you file a complaint with the PSC. If you never file a complaint then people are left in the dark about how they operate.

I would hope that for everyone that has a complaint about them to file a complaint. I have learned that they only have one person handling complaints from their end. Don't let them tell you that T-Netix and Evercom are one and the same company. They tried to pull that with me. Each of them have a separate tariff on file with the PSC.  I do not like saying things about people that are not good, but I can tell you from personal experience that these csr's do not know what they are talking about.

Another thing please send a letter of complaint to this gentleman at DBM about T-NETIX. Ellis Kitchen, State Chief of Information Technology. MD DBM, 45 Calvert Street, Annapolis, MD 21401-1907. They do take these complaints serious.

Please let me know if you could check your Verizon bill and let me know what your monthly bill statement fee is. It should be $1.95.
